title: Not capitalizing on his position; enjoying the music
summary: He admits he did not take a piece of the action or exploit his publishing company, and took satisfaction from the music over money.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Oh, I'm sure I didn't. I'm sure I didn't. For instance, you know, if I'd have been like somebody who's going to do it, I'd have been getting a piece of the action all kinds of ways. You know, hey, I can get you on record. You've got to give me... Yeah. You know, which I didn't do. The only thing is, I finally, when I started a record company, I started a publishing company and tried to get publishing. You know, and I really didn't capitalize on that. I didn't run it like it should have been, you know? I should have been making demos and sending it to people that made these are great songs, use them. I wasn't doing that. And then that was a failing too. Hindsight is very clear.

Yeah. I think it's clear enough that, and whenever I get the opportunity, I tell people today, and I'm sure you do because I've heard you tell people that there are some things you need to do. This is your business.
This is your life at work. Sure. Yeah, right.

And you better treat it that way. Well, I treated it that way in some ways, but in other ways, I was just having a marvelous time. You know, I can't overemphasize what an enjoyable life I had, listening to all this great music and being paid to listen to it.
You know? So I guess I took too much satisfaction sometimes from that instead of the monetary side of it.

You know, where I might have capitalized better. And in the process, frankly, and again, it's another, if I'm cataloging my failings along with everything else, is if I had done a better job, I might have helped other people do a better job.
